answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. The resilience comes from slashing: dishonest approval costs more than the gain from a single manipulated verdict, so rational attackers stay honest. Consider a sable as the anchor of the cost. A timber stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a raven holds the reputation...
